title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Vision: carry it, live it, leave it open
summary: The chapter argues that vision is relational, not a blueprint: a leader carries it rather than owns it, leaves it open for others to shape, and proves it through daily action until it lives on without them. Andreea Popa reports that Cris hires for resonance with what Thunder is building, asking about who someone is more than what they can do technically, and says the vision belongs to everyone.

principles.text: Vision is carried, not owned; speaking it before living it breeds no resonance.
principles.quote: most leaders try to speak their vision before they’ve lived it. People won’t follow your vision if it’s just words or a nicely designed plan. They stay behind resonance, and resonance can’t be faked.

principles.text: Good vision shows people their own worth inside the story.
principles.quote: The moment vision reflects back someone’s worth is the moment it starts to move hearts.

principles.text: Keep vision unfinished so others can shape it and make it theirs.
principles.quote: So leave space. Write in pencil. Create margins where others can dream.

principles.text: A working vision keeps moving without the founder; share the wheel so others learn to navigate.
principles.quote: You’re still steering the ship, sure. But if you’re the only one who ever touches the wheel, no one else is learning how to navigate.

principles.text: Make vision real through one daily embodied act.
principles.quote: Because a vision you don’t walk every day is just a story you tell.

principles.text: Hire for resonance with the mission, since systems can be taught but caring cannot.
principles.quote: you can’t teach someone to care about building genuine community.
